title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). f: X -> Y is a morphism. T -> Y is a 'base' given with a lift T -> X, equivalently a section of X_T = X x_Y T over T. T plays the role of a generalized base point (a geometric point, or a simply connected scheme such as a universal cover). E^T_X denotes the profinite fundamental group of X based at T, and E^T_{X/Y} the relative fundamental group. Under a universal 'homotopy exact sequence' hypothesis, Grothendieck had obtained (12) E^T_{X/Y} = pi_1(X_T; T) and the exact sequence (13) 1 -> E_{X/Y} -> E_X -> E_Y -> 1. That sequence holds, for instance, when Y = Spec K and X is geometrically connected over K.

This page drops the surjectivity of E_X -> E_Y.

(14) There is a canonical factorization X -> Y' -> Y. Here Y' is the finite étale, or more generally pro-finite-étale, cover of Y attached to the closed image subgroup of E_X in E_Y. This is the 'étale part of a Stein factorization' at the level of pi_1. After this replacement, E_X -> E_{Y'} is an epimorphism.

(15) Since E_{Y'} -> E_Y is injective, the kernels agree: E^T_{X/Y} = E^T_{X/Y'}.

(16) Applying the exact-sequence result to X/Y' gives E^T_{X x_{Y'} T} = E^T_{X/Y}. T maps to Y' through its lift to X.

Grothendieck then warns that X_T = X x_Y T is no longer the right object. It equals X x_{Y'} (Y' x_Y T). When T is simply connected, Y' x_Y T is a disjoint union of copies of T indexed by the fibre of Y' -> Y. So X_T is disconnected, and the relevant piece is the component X x_{Y'} T containing the given section.

He then begins to specialize T: take T = Y~, the universal cover of Y, in place of X_T, and X~ for the analogue of X_{Y~}. On the next page this yields (17) E_{X/Y} = Ker(E_X -> E_Y). With T a geometric point it yields (19): E_{X/Y} is the fundamental group of the geometric fibres.

Purpose: to set up relative fundamental groups and homotopy exact sequences with flexible base points. This is groundwork for the anabelian / Galois-action formalism of the Longue Marche, where Y = Spec K and the relative group is the geometric fundamental group.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The identification of X x_{Y'} T with a connected component of X_T silently assumes T is (pro-)simply connected, or at least that Y' x_Y T splits over T. The page only gestures at this ('qui est ... si Y'->Y ...').

Identifying Ker(E_X -> E_Y) with the fundamental group of the fibre over Y' still needs the exactness hypothesis (e.g. proper/flat with geometrically reduced fibres) for X -> Y'. This hypothesis is assumed, not proved.

ideas.what: Canonical factorization X -> Y' -> Y through the (pro-)finite étale cover corresponding to the image of pi_1(X) in pi_1(Y), so that pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y') becomes surjective.
ideas.modern_name: Étale part of the Stein factorization / pro-étale cover associated with the image subgroup
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. IX §5 and Exp. X (homotopy exact sequence, Stein factorization)

ideas.what: Relative fundamental group E^T_{X/Y} is unchanged by passing to Y', and equals pi_1 of the base change X x_{Y'} T, with care that X x_Y T is disconnected.
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y) and the homotopy exact sequence for fibrations with non-connected fibres

ideas.what: Fundamental groups based at a simply connected 'base' T (universal cover, geometric point) rather than a point, used uniformly to compare relative groups.
ideas.modern_name: Base points as fibre functors / pro-objects (universal covers as base points); fundamental groupoid with generalized base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 1 Exp. V), later Deligne (tangential base points, 1989)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. V; discussion in La Longue Marche (1981)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but standard bookkeeping of SGA 1 material: the Stein-type factorization of the pi_1 map, the relative fundamental group as a kernel, and base points as simply connected schemes. It is preparation for the Longue Marche formalism, with nothing that goes beyond the published record.
transcription_corrections: The formula after (14) reads '\mathcal{E}_X \to \mathcal{E}_{Y'}' (no prime on E_X), i.e. the map to the fundamental group of Y'.
In (16) the subscript is X x_{Y'} T (the fibre product of X and T over Y'), not 'X_{Y'}T' in the sense of a base change of X_T.
'pro-étale-fini' is better read as 'pro-étale fini sur Y'.
The passage after (16) reads roughly: 'faisons attention que maintenant X_T diffère en général de X x_{Y'} T (qui en est une composante si ... Y' -> Y ...), mais X x_{Y'} T'.
The last lines read roughly: '... T par \tilde Y pour ce qui concerne X_T, et par \tilde X pour ce qui est de l'analogue des X_{\tilde Y}', which continues on the next page with the universal covers.
